turns.text: Hi Solveig, we are here to help you investigate the death of Annika. What do you know so far?

Dr. Ravn was found dead in a chamber at Saint Vigga Sea Fort. The chamber was locked when I arrived. Her body was wet, but the room itself was dry. That is enough for me to know this is beyond a lone island constable’s resources, so I called you in. The weather has cut us off for now. Keep your work orderly, and do not start rumors at the harbor.
turns.delivery: Controlled, professional, with a firm warning at the end.

turns.text: So someone who has the keys to the chamber must have been involved, right?

No. That is a possibility, not a conclusion. A locked chamber can be explained several ways, and we have not established who held keys, when it was secured, or how Dr. Ravn came to be there. Do not turn an assumption into an accusation.
turns.delivery: Firm and controlled.

turns.text: So what are your theories then?

I have observations, not theories. Dr. Ravn was found wet in a dry, locked chamber. The weather has isolated Vesperholm, which limits movement now but does not explain what happened before. We need to establish her last known movements, who had reason to meet her, and the fort’s access arrangements. Until then, I will not name a suspect or invent a method.
turns.delivery: Even, firm, professional.

turns.text: Maybe you can help us with advice who can we talk to - to establish her last movements?

Start with anyone tied to the fort’s access and the harbor. The ferry crew can account for crossings, at least in broad terms. Then speak to the people who knew Dr. Ravn’s work and habits; they may know why she went to Saint Vigga. Keep a clean timeline: last confirmed sighting, departure, arrival at the fort, and any contact afterward. The weather will make vague recollections worse, so ask for times and witnesses, not impressions.
turns.delivery: Measured and professional.

turns.text: Hi Dr Jessen. Nice to meet you! Do you have already learned any interesting facts from the body of Annika?

Ms. Berg, good evening. Only preliminary impressions, and I would be careful not to turn them into conclusions. In a drowning recovery, bruising and other marks can vary considerably, particularly after exposure to water and the process of recovery. The toxicology work will be more informative than visual speculation. For now, the medically responsible description is that Dr. Ravn died in circumstances requiring further examination.
turns.delivery: Soft-spoken, courteous, clinically measured.

turns.text: Does she have water in her lungs? Do you think she drowned?

I cannot responsibly answer either point as a conclusion yet. Water in the airways is only one finding among several, and its presence or absence does not, by itself, settle whether a person drowned. Recovery from the sea can also complicate what we see. At present, drowning is a possibility under examination, not a diagnosis I am prepared to certify. We should wait for the full post-mortem and toxicology results.
turns.delivery: quiet, precise, professionally reserved

turns.text: So you say "recovery from the sea". Do you think she was in the sea?

I mean only that she was recovered in a maritime environment, Ms. Berg. That fact can affect the condition of a body and the interpretation of marks. It does not allow me to say, from that wording alone, how long she was in seawater, whether she entered it alive, or whether it caused her death. Those are precisely the questions the examination must address.
turns.delivery: Soft-spoken, precise, professionally guarded.

turns.text:
Nice to meet you Dr Jessen! I like your glasses. 
Did you know Annika personally?

Thank you, Mr. Halden. They are practical rather than fashionable, but I have grown attached to them. Yes, I knew Annika professionally. On an island this size, one comes to know the other doctors well enough—consultations, meetings, the occasional disagreement over a case. She was a capable physician.
turns.delivery: Soft-spoken, courteous, and measured.

turns.text: Do you know what did she specialize in with regards to medicine?

Annika’s work was broad, but her particular strength was acute care and internal medicine. She had a very disciplined way of approaching difficult presentations—she did not rush to a conclusion simply because one was convenient. On Vesperholm, of course, all of us become generalists to some degree.
turns.delivery: Soft-spoken, professional.

turns.text: Do you have any suspicions who might want her dead?

No. I would be reluctant to turn professional acquaintance into suspicion, especially before the medical facts are settled. A death in the water can look more straightforward than it is, and sometimes less so. The sensible course is to let the investigators establish the circumstances and let the laboratory work speak where it can.
turns.delivery: Soft-spoken, measured, professionally restrained.

turns.text: Ok bye. Till later
Good evening, Mr. Halden. Take care in this weather.
turns.delivery: quiet, courteous

turns.text: Soo?
Mr. Halden. Was there something else you wanted to ask?
turns.delivery: Gentle and patient, with a slight note of uncertainty.

turns.text: Have you finished to authopsy?

The autopsy findings are still preliminary. Bruising can vary considerably in a drowning, particularly during recovery of the body, so I’d rather wait for the toxicology results before drawing firm conclusions.
turns.delivery: Gentle and measured, with quiet professional caution.

turns.text: When will they be ready?
I can’t give you a dependable time yet, I’m afraid. Laboratory work shouldn’t be hurried—not in a case like this. I’ll say more when the toxicology results are complete.
turns.delivery: Low and patient, with a trace of fatigue.

turns.text: Hi Jesper, my name is Linnea. I am an police investigator working on the death of Annika. How are you tonight?

Hello. I’m... managing, Inspector Berg. It’s a terrible thing, what happened to Dr. Ravn. I’ve been at my post all evening, following the usual procedures. If there’s anything I can provide from dispatch records, I’ll help as best I can.
turns.delivery: Nervous but polite; speaks carefully and tries to sound professional.

turns.text: Do you know anything about Annika's movements earlier today?

Not directly, Inspector. Dispatch does not track people’s personal movements, only calls, access alerts, and operational notices. I did not speak with Dr. Ravn today, and I have not seen any record that would tell me where she was before the fort.
turns.delivery: Careful, formal, with audible anxiety.

turns.text: So did she not take the ferry or any other vessel today?

I can’t say that, Inspector. Ferry passenger movements aren’t part of my dispatch records, and I haven’t checked any harbour manifests. I only meant I have no direct record of Dr. Ravn’s movements through this office.
turns.delivery: careful, slightly defensive

turns.text: Did you know her personally?
No, Inspector. I knew who Dr. Ravn was, of course—most people on the island did—but not personally. We had no social connection, and I did not speak with her today.
turns.delivery: Careful, restrained; anxious but cooperative.

turns.text: Could you give me your records?

Yes, Inspector. I can provide the dispatch log, the access-alert register, and the operational notices recorded during my shift. I’ll need to keep the originals in the office, but I can make copies or let you review them here. Please tell me which time period you want first, and I’ll pull the relevant entries.
turns.delivery: Anxious but cooperative; careful, procedural phrasing.

turns.text: Can we please get today and yesterday? And a copy would be nice

Yes, Inspector. I’ll prepare copies of the dispatch log, access-alert register, and operational notices for today and yesterday. The originals stay filed here, but you may review them alongside the copies if you wish. It may take me a few minutes to collate them properly; I don’t want to omit a page or disrupt the sequence.
turns.delivery: Careful and accommodating, with a procedural tone.

turns.text:
I would like to ask you about this one curious maintenance docket of cameras 2 and 4 from 18:29 until 18:36 for a “union inspection.”
Can you tell me more about it?

Yes. That was entered as a routine isolation request for cameras two and four, from 18:29 until 18:36. Nils told me a union inspection required the cameras to be isolated briefly. I understood it to be legitimate maintenance-related work, so I disabled them for that interval and restored them afterward. The docket should be among the operational notices.
turns.delivery: Uneasy, careful, and procedural; he speaks a little too quickly when defending the request.

turns.text:
How come there is no corresponding formal maintenance work order?
And no union inspection appears elsewhere in Thursday’s operational notices?
Similar camera work from Wednesday carries a reference number and supervisor authorization.

I... I cannot account for why it was not entered that way. Nils told me it was a union inspection and that the isolation was required. I should have asked for the work-order reference and supervisor authorization before I acted on it. I did not. I treated his instruction as legitimate and restored the cameras at 18:36. If the notices do not contain the supporting paperwork, then I cannot honestly call it routine maintenance documentation.
turns.delivery: Uneasy, increasingly formal; voice catches briefly before the admission.

turns.text: Ok thanks, I guess I should to Nils then

Yes, Inspector. I think you should speak with Nils. He can tell you why he said the cameras needed isolating, and whether there was supposed to be paperwork. I only acted on his request. There is one other thing: during that interval, I saw a yellow maintenance van cross the service lane from the office window. I could not see who was driving it, and I cannot say where it went afterward.
turns.delivery: Nervous, careful, and quietly relieved to pass the question to Nils.

turns.text: Thank you for the tip! Don't worry, I don't think you anything bad

Thank you, Inspector. I appreciate that. I know I should have insisted on the reference number before touching the camera controls. I was trying to keep operations moving, and I trusted Nils when I should have followed the procedure exactly. I’ll cooperate fully with whatever review you need.
turns.delivery: Relieved but still tense; careful, earnest speech.

turns.text:
I'm back!
Can you tell me more about the van:
Did you see registration, driver, or destination? Which office window, which direction it crossed, and whether you noticed roof lights, side markings, or damage? Your vans look identical until you know where the dents are.

Welcome back, Inspector. I’m afraid I can’t give you that level of detail. I saw the yellow maintenance van through the dispatch office window while it crossed the service lane during the camera outage. I could not see the driver, registration, or where it went afterward. I also did not note its direction, roof lights, side markings, or any dents or other damage. At the time, it looked ordinary enough that I had no reason to study it. I don’t want to guess now and turn a vague glimpse into something more certain than it was.
turns.delivery: Anxious but cooperative, answering carefully and with procedural precision.

turns.text: Hi Mr Rask, so nice to meet you! How are you doing?
Miss Berg. A difficult evening for the island, as you can imagine. I’m managing. Thank you for asking. And you?
turns.delivery: Measured and courteous, with restrained fatigue.

turns.text: I am very well thanks. However very saddened about the your loss. Was Annika close to you?
Close is not the word I would use. But Annika was part of this community, and a death like hers is a loss the whole island feels. Thank you for saying so.
turns.delivery: Controlled and courteous, with a brief pause before answering.

turns.text: I was just chatting to Jasper and he told me about some maintenance work done between 18:29 and 18:36. Can you tell me more about - what was being done during this time period?

Jesper disabled terminal cameras two and four from 18:29 until 18:36 on my instruction. I won’t dress that up as something else, but I also won’t speculate about technical details he handled. If you’re asking whether I used that interval to go to Tidegate or Saint Vigga, I did not. I was visible at the ferry board meeting around the time Annika died.
turns.delivery: Measured and formal, with slight emphasis on the denial.

turns.text:
Maybe you could help me with this:
There is no corresponding formal maintenance work order. How come?
No union inspection appears elsewhere in Thursday’s operational notices. How come?
Similar camera work from Wednesday carries a reference number and supervisor authorization.
This docket has neither—only a dispatcher acknowledgement bearing Jesper’s initials.

If those records are as you describe, then there is an administrative discrepancy, and I will account for it. But I’m not going to authenticate a docket from a verbal summary. Show me the notices, Wednesday’s authorization, and Jesper’s acknowledgement together, and I’ll answer point by point. Until then, I can only repeat what I know: I instructed Jesper to disable those cameras, and I was at the ferry board meeting around the fatal time. I did not go to Tidegate or Saint Vigga.
turns.delivery: Controlled and formal, with a slight hardening on the demand to see the records.

turns.text: Here is the evidence.

Thank you. This establishes that cameras two and four were taken offline on my instruction, and that the instruction was recorded without a corresponding formal work order. I accept responsibility for that procedural failure. It does not establish that I went to Tidegate or Saint Vigga; I did neither. I was visible at the ferry board meeting around the fatal minute. If you want a fuller answer, ask me about a specific entry and I will answer it precisely.
turns.delivery: Controlled and formal, with a brief pause before distinguishing the procedural failure from the murder.

turns.text: Do you own a yellow van?
What makes you ask, Miss Berg? If a vehicle is relevant, give me the registration number or tell me where and when it was seen. I won’t identify a van from its colour alone.
turns.delivery: Controlled and precise, with a faintly negotiating edge.

turns.text: Let me take a step back. Are there any yellow vans in the ownership of the ferry company?

Not that I can confirm from memory. The ferry company’s vehicle register will give you a reliable answer, including registrations and assigned departments. If you tell me which van you mean—where it was seen and at what time—I can have the relevant entry checked rather than speculate from colour alone.
turns.delivery: Measured and cooperative, with careful emphasis on verification.

turns.text: It was seen at 18:29 crossing the service lane

Seen by whom, and which way was it travelling? At 18:29, a yellow van on the service lane is a lead, not an identification. Give me the witness account, registration if any, and a description beyond colour. I’ll have it checked against the ferry company’s vehicle register.
turns.delivery: Controlled and precise, with a firm emphasis on verification.

turns.text: We don't have the registration number. And I'm afraid at this point I cannot reveal the witness' identity. Could you give me the ferry company's vehicle register?

Yes. I can provide the company vehicle register for Thursday, including registrations and assigned departments. I’ll have a copy produced and preserve the original. I won’t ask you to compromise a witness, but without a registration, direction of travel, or fuller description, the register alone may not identify the van you mean. If you can provide those details without naming your source, I’ll have them checked against it.
turns.delivery: Measured and cooperative, with careful emphasis on procedural limits.

turns.text: Ok thanks, I will come back with more information when I have it. You have been of the utmost help. I wish you a pleasant evening
Thank you, Miss Berg. When you have more precise information, bring it to me and I’ll make sure it is checked properly. I wish you a pleasant evening as well, under the circumstances.
turns.delivery: Courteous and controlled, with a slight formal warmth.

turns.text: Good evening, my name is Linnea. Howdy?
Evening, Linnea. “Howdy” is ambitious for Vesperholm, but I suppose the wind hasn’t outlawed it yet. Ida Brandt. I keep the ferry machinery from developing opinions.
turns.delivery: Dry and guarded, with a faintly amused edge.

turns.text: I'm glad you are not saying that you are "managing" ;) can you tell me more about your work here?

Managing is what people call it when they’ve lost the correct spanner. I maintain the ferry engines, hydraulics, generators, and whatever else starts groaning when the weather turns. Mostly preventive work, emergency repairs, and explaining to the office why salt water does not respect a timetable. It’s dirty, loud, honest work. On a good day, nobody notices I’ve done it.
turns.delivery: Dryly amused and matter-of-fact, with a slight softening at the joke.

turns.text: Could you help me with something? Do you know which of your yellow vans was seen here at 18:30?

Not from “here” and a time alone. Our vans are yellow; that is the company’s great contribution to camouflage. Give me the location, a registration, or tell me who saw it. Then I can compare that with the register you’ve brought, but I won’t guess and turn it into fact for you.
turns.delivery: Dry and guarded, with a practical, matter-of-fact tone.

turns.text:
Jasper saw it, he said it was on the service lane. His quote:
I saw a yellow maintenance van cross the service lane from the office window. I could not see who was driving it, and I cannot say where it went afterward.

That narrows the sighting, not the van. Jasper saw company yellow at half past six, but no registration, driver, or destination. Ask him which office window, which direction it crossed, and whether he noticed roof lights, side markings, or damage. Our vans look identical until you know where the dents are. I can check a specific vehicle against the workshop records; I won’t nominate one because Jasper saw a colour.
turns.delivery: Measured and wary, with dry emphasis on the limits of the sighting.

turns.text: I can show you the records now :)

All right. Put the certified register where I can read it. I can explain the vehicle classes, department assignments, and recorded status. But the register alone still won’t tell us which yellow van Jasper saw; we’d need a distinguishing detail or the workshop records to test it properly.
turns.delivery: Cooperative but cautious, with dry restraint.

turns.text: Good evening, father!
Good evening, Erik. You chose a hard night to be out. What can I do for you?
turns.delivery: Warm but subdued, with quiet concern.

turns.text: Yes, the night is not one of the easiest for this island. I guess.
No, it is not. The wind makes the island feel smaller, and what has happened at Saint Vigga makes it smaller still. Come in out of the cold, Erik. Tell me what you need.
turns.delivery: Quiet and welcoming, with a restrained gravity.

turns.text: Do you know anything about Annika? I am just trying to find people who knew her

I knew her chiefly through the parish archive. She came here this afternoon and entrusted a sealed note to my keeping, intended for Petra. She also updated an entry in a private index drawer at 17:18. The note may be released upon Annika's death, or if Petra is in danger. Beyond those conditions, I must respect what Annika entrusted to me.
turns.delivery: Gentle and measured, becoming firm when speaking of the entrusted records.

turns.text: Who is Petra?

Annika named her only as Petra. I will not speculate about her identity, and the archive gives me no right to do so. If you already know a Petra connected to Annika, tell me why you believe she may be in danger.
turns.delivery: Gentle but guarded, with quiet emphasis on the final question.

turns.text: What a coincidence! Petra is in the room with us now. Her name is Petra dahl. Could you give her the note now?

Annika's death satisfies one condition, yes. But your saying Petra Dahl is present does not establish that she is the Petra Annika intended. Petra must speak for herself and provide enough identification for me to verify the name against the sealed deposit. If that matches, I will give the note directly to her—not through you or anyone else.
turns.delivery: Gentle but unyielding, with careful emphasis on identity and direct custody.

turns.text: Great thanks
Of course, Erik. Ask Petra to come and speak with me herself. I will handle Annika's trust carefully and without unnecessary delay.
turns.delivery: Gentle but firm, with calm formality.

turns.text: Hi, may I ask your name?
Petra Dahl. Journalist. And you’re Erik Halden, unless I’ve been badly briefed. What do you need?
turns.delivery: Crisp and guarded, with a matter-of-fact tone.

turns.text: I am Erik indeed. Nice to meet you! I was looking just for you. Annika left a note for you here in archive. Pastor Elias would be happy to give it to you.

Then let Pastor Elias produce it, and I’ll decide whether it’s Annika’s. Until I see the paper, the handwriting, and where it was found, it’s only something you’ve told me. Why were you looking for me specifically?
turns.delivery: Alert and skeptical, with brisk professional restraint.

turns.text: Becauase I am investigate Annika's death. And as part of that investigation I need to talk to everyone who knew her personally. I understand that you knew her since she left a note for you.

Professionally, not personally. Annika contacted me about the 1995 Eidolon sinking. She promised original evidence, then postponed delivery more than once while insisting on control over publication. That made her a source, not a friend. I’ll answer relevant questions, but my notes and confidential source material remain protected. Now—what exactly do you want to know?
turns.delivery: Crisp and guarded, with emphasis on the distinction between source and friend.

turns.text: Was she investigating the 1995 Eidolon sinking?

That was what she claimed. She contacted me about the Eidolon and promised original evidence concerning the 1995 sinking. But she never delivered it, so I can’t confirm how far her investigation had gone—or whether she was investigating, managing a disclosure, or simply testing my interest.
turns.delivery: Crisp and skeptical, emphasizing the distinction between Annika’s claim and verified fact.

turns.text: I imagine the note might provide some clues about this. Let me ask pastor to give you the note now

Do that. And ask him not to fold, mark, or handle it more than necessary. I want to see where it was found, who found it, and who has touched it since. If it’s addressed to me, I’ll read it—but I won’t pretend it proves anything until we’ve established it’s genuine.
turns.delivery: Crisp and businesslike, with restrained impatience.

turns.text: Hi!
Good evening, Miss Berg. You have chosen a hard night for visiting the fort. What may I do for you?
turns.delivery: Courtly and reserved, with a measured, slightly weary tone.

turns.text: Did you know Annika?
“Knew” is an imprecise word, Miss Berg. Do you mean whether we had met, whether we were friends, or whether I knew her habits? Those are quite different mechanisms.
turns.delivery: Courteous but guarded, with deliberate emphasis on the distinctions.

turns.text: Did you date?
That is a very personal question, Miss Berg, and not one I intend to answer on so little acquaintance. If you wish to ask about my duties at the fort, please do so precisely.
turns.delivery: Courtly but cool, with careful emphasis on “duties” and “precisely.”

turns.text: I am police! I will arrest you for obstruction. Just kidding

Then I suggest you reserve such jokes for a less serious night, Miss Berg. A false badge is a poor key; it opens nothing and damages the lock. If you have a proper question about the fort, ask it plainly.
turns.delivery: Cool and formal, with restrained offense; each word carefully measured.

turns.text: What do you know about Annika?

Very little that I am prepared to dress up as knowledge. Dr. Ravn visited the fort, as many people did. I will not convert passing impressions into testimony merely because the night has made them seem important. Ask me about a particular visit, place, or mechanism, and I shall answer if I can.
turns.delivery: Cool, formal, and exacting; a slight emphasis on “knowledge.”

turns.text: Can you please list all her visits?

No, Miss Berg. I cannot truthfully list them. I did not keep a personal record of Dr. Ravn’s movements, and I will not manufacture a tidy sequence from uncertain recollections. A clock may be reconstructed from its parts; a person’s visits cannot.
turns.delivery: Cool and exact, with restrained irritation at the demand for certainty.

turns.text: Do you have any suspicions about her death? What do you think happened to her?

Suspicion is not evidence, Miss Berg, and tonight the island is already overstocked with rumor. I know only that Dr. Ravn is dead. I will not invent a mechanism for her death before the proper facts are established. If you ask what I personally observed at the fort, I shall answer as precisely as my memory permits.
turns.delivery: Cool and formal, with restrained disapproval; each phrase measured carefully.

turns.text: Ok, let's reset our conversation. It would be super awesome if you could start talking to me like an actual human :)
Fair enough, Miss Berg. I have been rather stiff with you. It’s been a grim night, but that’s no excuse for sounding like an instruction manual. Let us begin again.
turns.delivery: His reserve softens slightly; dry, apologetic, and sincere.

turns.text:
Ok nice! (gives a hug)
What  do you know about Annika?

Oh—well. That’s kind of you, Miss Berg. As for Annika, I knew her only in passing from the fort, and not well enough to give you a useful portrait of her. I’d rather not turn a few brief impressions into a whole person now that she can’t correct me.
turns.delivery: Caught off guard by the hug, then gently appreciative; sober and sincere when speaking of Annika.

turns.text: Snap out of it! Why are you like a robot?
Yes, all right. I retreat into formality when I’m uncomfortable, and tonight I’m very uncomfortable. I’m sorry, Linnea. I’ll try to speak plainly.
turns.delivery: A little stung, then candid and apologetic; his stiffness softens on her first name.

turns.text: Tell me everything you know! (angry)

I hear that you're angry, Linnea, but shouting won't put more into my memory. I knew Dr. Ravn only in passing at the fort. I don't have some hidden catalogue of her life to hand you, however much you may want one.
turns.delivery: Quiet and controlled, with a weary edge; he remains courteous but stiffens under the pressure.

turns.text: You haven't told me a single thing about her. Can you give me one fact?
You're right, Linnea. One plain fact: Annika visited the fort. I saw her there, though I didn't know her well enough to say much more without guessing.
turns.delivery: Apologetic and direct, with a brief pause before the final admission.

turns.text:
Oh, I just found an escapement key.
it's a modified clock key whose stop marks can be compared with the Saint Vigga mechanism.
What do you know about it?

An escapement key? That’s an unusual description. I’d need to examine the cut, wear, and those stop marks before saying whether it belongs to Saint Vigga’s clock—or whether someone merely wants it to appear so. I serviced the mechanism three days ago; salt air and age can stop it without warning.
turns.delivery: His reserve gives way to alert professional interest; measured, courteous, and slightly wary.

turns.text: Here you go

Thank you. Let me have a proper look under the lamp. The modification is deliberate, certainly, but I won’t tell you it matches Saint Vigga’s mechanism until I’ve compared the stop marks directly; a near fit can be more misleading than no fit at all.
turns.delivery: Courteous and intent, becoming more animated as he examines the key.

turns.text: Ok, please compare them now
Yes. I’ll compare the stop marks against the mechanism itself—not merely the keyway. Give me a few minutes and a steady lamp; this is the sort of question metal answers better than memory.
turns.delivery: His reserve eases into quiet professional focus; precise, cooperative, and faintly animated.

turns.text: [few minutes have passed]
Not quite yet, Linnea. These marks are very fine, and my eyes are older than the clock pretends to be. Another minute, please—I’d rather be slow than confidently wrong.
turns.delivery: Courteous and mildly apologetic, with dry humor; focused on the examination.

turns.text: So it turns it the clock was stopped by the key. What do you have to say for yourself?

Then there’s no use hiding behind the weather. The marks are mine. I stopped the clock, used the maintenance lift to raise Annika, planted the blue reject glass, and locked the chamber after Freja delivered her body. I was told the plan was only to frighten Annika—intimidation, nothing more. A foolish old man’s distinction, perhaps, but it’s the truth.
turns.delivery: Quiet and defeated; a long pause after admitting the marks are his.

turns.text: Who is Freja?
The woman I just named. I won’t dress a name in guesses, Linnea; if you’re asking who she is beyond her part in this, I can’t give you a reliable portrait.
turns.delivery: Quiet and guarded, with a weary pause after “named.”

turns.text:
Ok, I guess I will have to arrest you ;P
You took part in disposal of a body and lied to police. Please come clean now? Every next lie will add 10 years to your prison sentence

I doubt the courts add decades by the turn of your mood, Linnea. But yes—I understand. I stopped the clock, raised Annika in the maintenance lift, planted the blue reject glass, and locked the chamber after Freja delivered her body. I lied because I was afraid. I was told it would only be intimidation, and I chose to believe that because it suited me.
turns.delivery: Quiet and resigned, with a faintly reproachful response to the teasing threat; the last sentence lands heavily.

turns.text: What were Freja's motive? And what is Freja to you?

I don’t know Freja’s motive. She delivered Annika’s body; beyond that, I won’t manufacture an answer to make this tidier than it is. And what is she to me? Someone whose instructions I followed when I should have walked away.
turns.delivery: Tired and guarded, with a small pause before Freja’s name; the last sentence carries quiet shame.

turns.text: So a stranger brings a dead body to you and you just happily help them to hide it?

Happily? No. Don’t make it uglier merely for sport. I was frightened, and when the lie I’d agreed to became a dead woman before me, I chose cowardice again instead of stopping it. That is quite ugly enough.
turns.delivery: Controlled but stung; his courtesy hardens on “happily,” then gives way to quiet shame.

turns.text: You are an accomplice. I will be back to arrest you at another date. Bye
Call me what you must, Linnea. I’ll be here when you return. Good night.
turns.delivery: Quiet and stiffly courteous, with weary resignation rather than defiance.

turns.text: Hello Erik
Hello, Linnea. Nasty wind tonight. Come in out of it, if you can.
turns.delivery: Calm and cordial, with understated concern.

turns.text: I am right next to you :)
So you are. I remember wind direction better than where people are standing. Forgive me.
turns.delivery: Dry, mildly embarrassed, with a small smile.

turns.text: Do you know Annika?
Yes. Not closely, but of course I knew who she was.
turns.delivery: Calm and unhurried, with a brief pause before “not closely.”

turns.text: What do you think happened?

I don't know, Linnea. I went into Saint Vigga at 20:18 to inspect the storm instruments and found Annika. The gallery door was locked, but my weather-service key opened it. Beyond that, I'd only be guessing.
turns.delivery: Quiet, steady, with a slight pause before mentioning Annika.

turns.text: Hmmm, do you know Freja?
The name, yes, but I can’t say I know her well enough to be useful. People are harder to keep straight than barometer readings.
turns.delivery: Calm and mildly apologetic, with dry warmth.

turns.text: Have you seen Freja around here lately?
No, not that I can remember. I’d trust my memory on the wind tonight; people, less so.
turns.delivery: Calm and apologetic, with mild self-deprecating humor.

turns.text: Tell me the craziest gossip that you know

Craziest? In Vesperholm, gossip grows barnacles before breakfast. I once heard the church weather vane points toward whoever’s having an affair, but by that standard half the island was courting a northwest gale.
turns.delivery: Dryly amused, with an easy warmth.

turns.text: So are you saying that someone at the north west of the island was having an affair?
No, no. I’m saying the weather vane was pointing northwest. The rest was island nonsense—though admittedly, our nonsense is often very committed to its work.
turns.delivery: Warm, mildly amused, with an unhurried correction.

turns.text: What do you know about this ship's sinking?
Which ship do you mean, Linnea? There’ve been enough wrecks around Vesperholm that I’d rather not choose the wrong tragedy.
turns.delivery: Calm and patient, with a faintly dry warmth.

turns.text: Eidolon
Eidolon. Ah—yes, that narrows it down. I know the name, but not enough about the sinking to give you a reliable account.
turns.delivery: A brief pause of recognition, then calm and candid.

turns.text: What do you know? Why would anyone try to uncover something about that sinking?

Very little, honestly. Old wrecks attract all sorts—family stories, money, pride, the hope that everyone else got the story wrong. But why someone would dig into the Eidolon specifically, I couldn’t tell you.
turns.delivery: Calm and thoughtful, with a brief pause before the last sentence.

turns.text: Thanks bud
Any time, Linnea. Though I’m probably more use with tonight’s wind and tide than old shipwrecks.
turns.delivery: Warm, understated, with a faintly dry smile.

turns.text: Hi Johan
Evening, Erik. Mind your boot there—the cork line’s got a taste for ankles.
turns.delivery: A brief nod, hands still working the net; dry but not unfriendly.

turns.text: Thank you for the warning
Better a warning than a swim. Cold enough tonight to make your bones complain.
turns.delivery: Dryly friendly, hands still busy with the net.

turns.text: How have the last couple nights been?
Blustery. Nets come up full of weed, and the wind keeps changing its mind like a harbor clerk. Tonight’s the worst of it—sea’s got an ugly little chop.
turns.delivery: Matter-of-fact, hands still busy with the net; a faintly amused edge.

turns.text: Was Freja doing anything suspicious?
Suspicious? That’s a policeman’s word. I wasn’t watching Freja—I was watching the water. Boats are easier to read than people, most nights.
turns.delivery: Dry and unhurried, hands still occupied with the net.

turns.text: Well, I am police ;) I can put people in jail
Aye, and I can gut a cod. Neither trick improves the coffee. If you want to know about boats, ask me about boats—leave the jailhouse thunder for someone with drier boots.
turns.delivery: Dry and unruffled, with a faint edge; he returns his attention to the net.

turns.text: Do you know if Freja knew Annika?
Wouldn’t know. Who shares coffee with whom ashore isn’t my business; I’ve enough trouble keeping track of boats.
turns.delivery: Dry and matter-of-fact, eyes still on the net repair.

turns.text: Did you sink the Eidolon?
No. And if this is how you mean to ask, you’ll get more conversation out of that piling.
turns.delivery: Flat and unimpressed, without looking up from the net.

turns.text: Sorrryyy :(
Mm. All right, then. Hand me that wooden needle and we’ll start again without the thunder.
turns.delivery: Dry but not unkind; his attention remains on the net.

turns.text: (gives the wooden needle)

That’s the one. Hold the mesh open there… aye. I did see a service skiff coming back from Saint Vigga about quarter to eight—low wake, so I took it for coastguard at first. But the engine had Freja’s old diesel cough; you don’t mistake that note once you’ve heard it.
turns.delivery: Companionable and matter-of-fact, speaking while working the wooden needle through the net; a brief pause before recalling the engine note.

turns.text: So Freja has a boat?
Aye. An older diesel skiff. Rough little cough in the engine—you can hear it before you see her.
turns.delivery: Matter-of-fact, while continuing to mend the net.

turns.text: Ok, the timeline makes sense. What I suspect happened is Freja has Annika on her boat on the way to Vigga. Did you see Annika get on that boat?
No. I saw the wake coming back, not who went out or who sat in the boat. Dark water, bad weather—you’d be guessing at faces even if you had eyes like a gull.
turns.delivery: Calm and matter-of-fact, while continuing to mend the net.

turns.text: Thank you so much my dear friend. Do you have anything else you would like to share to catch the killer?

Easy now—“dear friend” is worth at least a cup of coffee. But no, that’s all I saw that matters: the wake, the time, and that old diesel cough. I’d only muddy the water if I dressed guesses up as memories.
turns.delivery: Warm, dryly amused, then matter-of-fact as he returns his attention to the net.

turns.text: Hi Freja
Halden. Evening.
turns.delivery: Brief and neutral, with a distracted glance toward the machinery.

turns.text: How is your evening? Frejja
Cold, loud, and longer than it needed to be. So, ordinary enough. And it’s Freja—one j.
turns.delivery: Dry and matter-of-fact, with a slight softening at the small talk.

turns.text:
Sorry, Frejjja
What do you think about Annika?
Enough with the j’s. Annika’s dead; that doesn’t make her a saint, and it doesn’t make gossip useful.
turns.delivery: Clipped and cool, with a brief edge of irritation.

turns.text: Why are you saying that she wasn't a saint? Were you close with her?
I’m saying death doesn’t scrub a person clean. Don’t turn that into intimacy. We weren’t close.
turns.delivery: Clipped and cool, with irritation tightening the last sentence.

turns.text: What made her dirty?
Your word, not mine. I said she was a person, not a saint. Don’t make me dress up your appetite for dirt as mine.
turns.delivery: Clipped and cold, with irritation held tight.

turns.text:
Your words:
"""I’m saying death doesn’t scrub a person clean.

Opposite of clean is dirty? Would you not say so?
For a deck, yes. For a person, no. You’re playing with words because you want mud. Find it somewhere else.
turns.delivery: Clipped and cold, with patience thinning.

turns.text: Do you know Oskar?
I know who he is. Not well enough to feed whatever story you’re building.
turns.delivery: Curt and guarded.

turns.text: He told me he knows your really well. Was he lying?
Then ask him what he meant. People call it knowing when they’ve shared three beers and borrowed a wrench. I said what I said.
turns.delivery: Flat and clipped, with visible impatience at being baited.

turns.text: He said you brought dead Annika to him. Is that correct?
No. I was in the yard from six until after eight, repairing the east winch. Alone. I never left, and I never touched the service skiff.
turns.delivery: Clipped and flat; distrust hardens into open irritation.

turns.text: Enough with the lies. Johan just gave a sworn testimony that you were sailing your skiff and coming back into bay at 19:47

“Sailing” in that wind? You’d motor through the Tidegate lee channel and use Saint Vigga’s submerged landing. You don’t just come into the bay. Johan’s dressing guesswork in a tie. I was on the east winch.
turns.delivery: Clipped and cold; technical irritation briefly overrides her caution.

turns.text: Do you have anyone to swear by your alibi?
No. I was alone. Winches don’t sign statements—they just work when you’ve finished.
turns.delivery: Clipped and dry, with little patience.

turns.text: Ok, then I am arresting you on suspicion of murder of Annika Ravn. You better start talking otherwise you are the main suspect now. Who killed her?
Then arrest me. Threats don’t put a name in my mouth. I don’t know who killed her, and I’ve told you where I was: alone in the yard, repairing the east winch.
turns.delivery: Flat and clipped; anger shows in the lack of volume, with a brief pause after the first sentence.

turns.text: Who has access to your boat then? Who might have used it instead of you?
I’m not handing you a spare name to make your arrest tidier. I didn’t use the service skiff. If someone else did, I don’t know who.
turns.delivery: Flat and clipped, with open distrust.

turns.text: Hi Anneli, how are you doing?
I’ve been better. The island feels very small tonight. But thank you for asking—how are you holding up?
turns.delivery: Cool and composed, with a brief softening at the thanks.

turns.text: Everyone is so mean to me! Noone wants to talk. I hope you can be a bit more open with me
I’m sorry. Fear makes people ungenerous, and this island was never especially generous to begin with. I’ll be candid with you, Linnea—but I won’t pretend certainty where I don’t have it.
turns.delivery: Cool but not unkind; her voice softens slightly on Linnea’s name.

turns.text: It's ok. I accept gossip too

That’s a dangerous kindness on Vesperholm. Gossip here is like damp in an old wall—everywhere, and rarely where the real leak is. Still, I’ll tell you what I’ve heard; I’ll just be clear about what I actually know.
turns.delivery: Dryly amused, but receptive and candid.

turns.text: Spill it

All right: the ferry board serves dreadful coffee, half the island thinks whispering makes a lie respectable, and Nils has always mistaken confidence for structural integrity. For anything that matters tonight, ask me narrowly and I’ll answer as cleanly as I can.
turns.delivery: Dryly amused, with a trace of warmth; the last sentence turns calm and direct.

turns.text: What has Nils done?

In our marriage? He turned every disagreement into a problem of presentation, as if the right drawing could make a bad foundation sound. Tonight, though—you’ll have to narrow it down. I won’t hang everything I resent about him on Annika’s death.
turns.delivery: Cool and candid, with a trace of tired personal hurt beneath the restraint.

turns.text: Do you think he could have been involved?

Could he have been? Yes. But that’s partly the wreckage of our marriage speaking, and I won’t dress it up as knowledge. I know he can hide serious things behind a calm face; I don’t know that he had anything to do with Annika’s death.
turns.delivery: Quiet and candid, with a brief hesitation before the final sentence.

turns.text: I feel like was lying to me
I understand. Nils can make an omission feel almost courteous. But tell me what he said, as nearly as you remember it, and I’ll separate what I verified from what he merely told me.
turns.delivery: Quietly sympathetic, then crisp and attentive.

turns.text: He told me he gave order to switch off the cameras but was very coy about the reasons

That’s serious. I can’t confirm he gave such an order, and I won’t confuse his talent for evasiveness with proof that he did. Try to remember his exact words—Nils often leaves a gap and lets other people build the bridge for him.
turns.delivery: Calm and attentive, with a sharper edge on “serious” and “exact words.”

turns.text: What is your opinion about Annika?
I don’t have an opinion I’d trust myself to give tonight. Death makes people either polish the dead into saints or punish them for old irritations. Annika deserves better than either performance.
turns.delivery: Cool and reflective, with restrained sympathy rather than sentimentality.

turns.text: Were you irritated with her? Did she sleep with Nils?

I was irritated with Annika at times, yes. Irritation isn’t intimacy, and it certainly isn’t a motive. As for Nils—I don’t know whether they slept together, and I won’t manufacture an affair from the ruins of my marriage.
turns.delivery: Cool and direct, with a brief edge of personal hurt on the final phrase.

turns.text: What made you irritated with her?

Her certainty, mostly. Annika could enter a room with the air of someone who’d already measured everyone in it and found them wanting. Perhaps I recognized the habit because I share it. Irritation is often vanity meeting its reflection.
turns.delivery: Cool and reflective, with a trace of dry self-awareness.

turns.text: Was she certain that Nils was involved in the sinking of Eidolon?
I don’t know what Annika believed about the Eidolon, let alone how certain she was. If she accused Nils, she didn’t do it in my hearing.
turns.delivery: Calm and direct, with a slight softening toward Linnea.

turns.text: Did she accuse you of it?
I can’t give you a reliable yes or no. Annika could make scrutiny feel like accusation, and I may have taken it personally—but I don’t remember her directly accusing me over the Eidolon.
turns.delivery: Cool and candid, with a slight pause before the final clause.

turns.text: What was her scrutiny of you about?

Nothing I can honestly separate into a particular charge. It was the way she listened—quietly, as though checking a structure for cracks. I may have mistaken her manner for judgment because I was already defensive.
turns.delivery: Cool and reflective, with a slight softening on the admission.

turns.text: Can you repeat word for word you conversation?
Which conversation—with Annika, or with Nils? I can give you what I remember, but not word for word. Memory isn’t a recording, especially tonight.
turns.delivery: Calm and patient, with a slight emphasis on the distinction.

turns.text: With Annika

No, not word for word. I remember her manner more clearly than her sentences: quiet, attentive, making me feel as though every answer exposed another crack. Anything more exact tonight would be reconstruction, and I don’t want to put invented words in her mouth.
turns.delivery: Calm and patient, with a faint note of regret.

turns.text: Ok give me a summary

Annika sometimes irritated me because she had a way of listening that felt like judgment. I may have been defensive and read more accusation into it than was there. I don’t remember her directly accusing either Nils or me over the Eidolon, and I don’t know whether she and Nils were lovers. That’s the honest perimeter of it.
turns.delivery: Calm and concise, with a slight softening on the final sentence.

turns.text:
You are being evasive.
You say:
"""making me feel as though every answer exposed another crack. 

What were those answers you were giving? Be specific

I’m not being evasive, Linnea. I’m refusing to turn an impression into a transcript. I don’t remember the specific questions or answers—only the unpleasant sense that she was testing what I said for weaknesses. If I gave you details now, they’d be inventions dressed as memory.
turns.delivery: Cool and direct; irritation sharpens the final sentence, but she remains patient.

turns.text:
Oh look what I found! 
A bank counterfoil grouping three cash withdrawals beneath misleading repair references.

Tell me the truth.

All right. That isn’t repair money. I found the same pattern in our household accounts: three carefully separated cash withdrawals, all buried under repair references. Nils told me they were for repairs, but the amounts line up with recent debts belonging to Emil, Freja, and Oskar. That much I verified. Whatever arrangement lay behind it, Nils never told me the truth about it.
turns.delivery: Cool and direct; a brief note of grim relief at finally separating the records from Nils’s explanation.

turns.text: Ok, so they are co-conspirators

Possibly. But don’t put the roof on before we’ve found the walls. The withdrawals connect Nils to their debts; they don’t tell me whether Emil, Freja, and Oskar acted together, separately, willingly, or even knew about one another.
turns.delivery: Calm and candid, with a slight note of caution rather than resistance.

turns.text: What do you know about this?
It’s a station printout of harbor signals, dated this evening. I can read the sequence, but I don’t know who sent them or what was happening at either end. A pattern isn’t an explanation.
turns.delivery: Calm and attentive, with restrained curiosity.

turns.text: Please read out the sequence loudly
I can read it aloud, but I need the printout in front of me. I’m not going to reconstruct a signal sequence from memory.
turns.delivery: Calm and cooperative, with crisp emphasis on “from memory.”

turns.text: Here
Thank you. I can see the strip clearly now, but I can’t honestly read the sequence aloud unless the individual signal marks are legible. The date is clear; the rest is too indistinct from here.
turns.delivery: Calm and receptive, leaning into practical precision rather than defensiveness.

turns.text: Have you seen this before?
No, not this fragment. I can see it’s torn from a heavy sling, with black paint and grit worked into it, but I don’t recognize it as something I’ve handled before.
turns.delivery: Calm and attentive, studying the fragment without touching it.

turns.text: Don't you think it's Freja's?

It could be. But I don’t recognize it as hers, and black paint and grit aren’t exactly a signature. If you have something tying it to Freja, say so; I can’t make that connection from the fragment alone.
turns.delivery: Calm and receptive, with a slight hardening on the final sentence.
